episodes.205967: Higher moisture moved into New Mexico between an upper low off the coast of southern California and an upper high over northern Mexico. This higher moisture combined with an upper level disturbance moving quickly east along the southern end of an upper low over the northern and central Rockies resulting in the development of showers and thunderstorms across northern and central New Mexico. Storms across south central New Mexico resulted in an estimated 60 mph wind gust in Magdelena and a peak wind gust of 62 mph at the Phillips Hull mesonet on the White Sands Missile Range. Thunderstorms coalesced into a squall line as they moved across eastern NM during the early to mid-evening hours. Peak wind gusts of 69 mph at Melrose Range and 64 mph at the Roswell Air Center and a West Texas Mesonet near Endee in eastern Quay County were measured along the leading edge of this squall line. This line of showers and thunderstorms moved east into West Texas shortly thereafter.
episodes.205974: Scattered thunderstorms developing during the midday into the afternoon hours. One of the thunderstorms knocked down trees in Morgan County during the mid afternoon.
episodes.205994: Heavy rainfall impacted portions of Limestone and Madison Counties in Northern Alabama, with several roads temporarily barricaded due to floodwaters. In all, 3-5 inches of rain occurred in East Limestone and Northwest Madison Counties.
episodes.206013: A mid-level short wave trough moving across New Mexico initiated thunderstorms in central New Mexico on the afternoon of the 22nd. These storms encountered harsher conditions as they moved east into eastern New Mexico and West Texas where much drier air was present. These storms produced a strong outflow boundary which generated severe thunderstorm wind gusts near Happy (Swisher County).
episodes.206028: A convergence boundary set up along the Allegheny Front and allowed for scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms to produce locally heavy rainfall in portions of Huntingdon County during the evening hours of September 22, 2025. Nuisance flooding was reported in Huntingdon County where State Route 453 near the intersection of US Route 22 was closed due to flooding.
episodes.206029: Daytime heating during the afternoon and evening hours of September 23, 2025 allowed for convection to occur across portions of the Lower Susquehanna Valley in an environment with ample moisture and low steering flow aloft allowing for slow-moving thunderstorms. Thunderstorms produced a quick 3 to 4 inches of rainfall in Millersville, which prompted multiple instances of flash flooding in the vicinity of Millersville University.
episodes.206246: A stationary front across northern Arkansas and an approaching outflow boundary from the northwest led to the development of an MCS which led many areas receiving rainfall via training and multiple accounts of flash flooding.
episodes.206324: In the early afternoon of the 22nd, storms began developing off a east/west oriented boundary, south of I-70. The boundary soon filled with storms that produced hail up to 1.25 inches, 61 MPH winds, and flooding by the morning of the 23rd.  The largest hail reported fell in Sharon Springs, the strongest wind gust was in southern Sherman County, and the flooding happened Logan County.
episodes.206399: A front approached southern Missouri during the afternoon and evening hours of September 23. Several thunderstorms developed and moved across the area. Some storms produced damaging winds in Dallas and Webster counties. Several instances of flash flooding occurred across McDonald, Barry and Taney counties where 2-3 inches of rainfall occurred.
episodes.206542: Pre-dawn storms moved across north-central and northeast Kansas. One cluster of storms briefly produced strong outflow with locally gusty winds to around 55 to 60 mph that downed one tree.
episodes.206648: Between the very late evening of the 22nd and the early morning of the 24th, multiple severe convective regimes developed across the WFO Norman Forecast Area. This convective event was triggered by a slow-moving upper-level system and its associated lead impulses. Initially, thunderstorms formed a broken line as they traversed northern Oklahoma. The presence of a reservoir of instability increased the potential for wind damage for a short time, with the system weakening as it approached the I-35 corridor. By the early evening of the 23rd, another round of severe weather emerged along a trailing cold front across eastern and southeastern Oklahoma. The combination of sufficient wind shear and instability during this event resulted in large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.206964: Thunderstorms due to a cold front and upper level disturbance produced large hail and damaging winds to portions of southeast WI. A lightning fatality also occurred to a man on a hiking trail in the Township of Kewaskum.
episodes.206973: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across east central and southeastern Oklahoma during the late afternoon and evening of the 23rd, along and ahead of a cold front that moved through the region. The strongest storms produced large hail to half dollar size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.206974: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed into northwestern Arkansas from the northwest during the afternoon of the 23rd, and additional thunderstorms developed across the area during the late afternoon and evening as a cold front moved through the region. The strongest storms produced large hail to ping pong ball size and damaging wind gusts. Locally heavy rainfall from these thunderstorms produced some flash flooding.
episodes.207010: A boundary stretching across portions of Southeast Missouri resulted in thunderstorms with heavy rain during the early morning hours of the 23rd from Carter County southeastward to New Madrid. A broader area of rainfall arrived late morning which produced additional heavy rains. Flooding issues developed in Southeastern Carter County which received some of the higher totals from both rounds. Precipitable water values were around 1.8in. 850mb moisture transport was not particularly strong, but was pointed towards the NW to SE oriented early morning heavy rainfall line.
episodes.207124: A very weak disturbance utilized a marginally severe storm environment across the western Texas Panhandle during the evening hours of September 22, 2025. A broken line of storms developed over the higher terrain of New Mexico, maintaining just enough strength to produce a couple of low end severe wind gusts as the western Texas Panhandle near Hereford.
episodes.207216: An isolated thunderstorm developed along a slow-moving frontal boundary across northwest Iowa. Seasonally high instability (around 2000 J/kg MLCAPE) and weak shear led to very strong updrafts, producing large hail that caused significant damage to late season crops.
episodes.207398: A strong storm moved through Dubuque county, with heavy rain, and small hail ranging from pea to penny size on the 22nd of September, 2025.
episodes.207451: On the 22nd, an upper-level wave and associated cold front was passing into Kansas. Later into the night, storms fired along the surface boundary and accessed a moisture atmosphere with PWATS over an inch. Added on top of sufficient instability and cool 700 mb temperatures, upon initiation strong storms in a MCS resulted. Near the eastern border of the CWA, a robust rear inflow jet developed and created a localized area of severe winds. The storm complex then moved out of the area into Wichita's CWA.
episodes.207585: Scattered thunderstorms developed over southwestern South Dakota during the early evening hours of September 22nd. As thunderstorms tracked to the southeast into northwestern Cherry County, they became severe. Hail up to half dollar size and wind gusts up to 60 MPH were reported in the Merriman area.
episodes.207605: On the evening of September 22, 2025, atmospheric conditions favored the development of scattered thunderstorms along a frontal zone stretching from east-central Nebraska into western Iowa. This activity was primarily driven by the intensification of a southerly low-level jet and the associated moist advection to the east of a weak lee trough and surface low over the central High Plains. Forecast soundings showed ample buoyancy and elongated upper-level hodographs, which suggested the potential for organized convection, specifically splitting supercell clusters capable of producing large hail. The first notable severe weather report occurred west of Prague, Nebraska, at 7:26 PM CST, with a measured hailstone diameter of 1.75 inches. As the complex cluster of thunderstorms slowly tracked east into west-central Iowa, numerous additional reports of hailfall were documented throughout the evening in Saunders, Dodge and Platte counties in Nebraska, with measured and estimated stone sizes ranging from 0.75 to 1.75 inches in diameter.
episodes.207606: On the evening of September 22, 2025, atmospheric conditions favored the development of scattered thunderstorms along a frontal zone stretching from east-central Nebraska into western Iowa. This activity was primarily driven by the intensification of a southerly low-level jet and the associated moist advection to the east of a weak lee trough and surface low over the central High Plains. Forecast soundings showed ample buoyancy and elongated upper-level hodographs, which suggested the potential for organized convection, specifically splitting supercell clusters capable of producing large hail. The first notable severe weather report occurred west of Prague, Nebraska, at 7:26 PM CST, with a measured hailstone diameter of 1.75 inches. As the complex cluster of thunderstorms slowly tracked east into west-central Iowa, numerous additional reports of hailfall were documented throughout the evening in Saunders, Dodge and Platte counties in Nebraska and, with measured and estimated stone sizes ranging from 0.75 to 1.75 inches in diameter. One public report of hail estimated up to 1.00 inch in diameter was acquired from Harrison county, Iowa at 9:12 PM CST.
episodes.207626: Thunderstorms which developed in association with a late September cold front and a Great Plains upper trough generated a few hail producing thunderstorms along the Red River region of North Texas the evening of September 23.
episodes.207699: Thunderstorms produced gusty winds and thunderstorms near the coast.
episodes.207700: An elongated positively tilted upper trough extended through the Great Lakes into Northern New Mexico.  An 80 knot jet was also moving through New Mexico which resulted in strong wind shear and severe thunderstorms moving across Sierra and Otero counties with wind gusts up to 78 mph.
episodes.207785: A decaying surface frontal boundary and ample moisture helped support diurnal showers and storms over land in the afternoon and the coastal waters overnight and in the morning hours in late September.
episodes.207786: A decaying surface frontal boundary and ample moisture helped support diurnal showers and storms over land in the afternoon and the coastal waters overnight and in the morning hours in late September.
episodes.207794: A cluster of thunderstorms moved from northern Oklahoma into southern Kansas during the early morning hours of September 23rd. A report of damaging winds was relayed from Harper County.
episodes.207829: A low tracking north of eastern Utah and western Colorado pushed a boundary through the northern counties, helping to trigger numerous showers and thunderstorms. Moisture with this system was rather shallow, but training thunderstorms made up for the lack of moisture, leading to flash flooding potential over sensitive areas. This included the Lee Burn Scar in Rio Blanco County, where numerous debris flows ran on this day.
episodes.208287: Storms developed in late afternoon along a boundary across northern Iowa, then sunk south through the evening. Storms were able to organize into a more cohesive line with 2000+ J/kg of MLCAPE and around 30 kts of shear. Storms initially resulted in a number of quarter sized hail reports, then transitions to wind damage as the cold pool surged south ahead of the line through the evening.
episodes.208422: Two men were were reportedly killed by an afternoon lightning strike in far southern Highlands County.
